name: Ennion mold-blown glass vessel
summary: A glass jug signed by Ennion had its body blown into a four-part mold, with the neck and base formed separately.
description: A signed glass jug with a body blown into a four-part mold and a separately formed neck and base.
tier_reason: Prefer a bounded product/process witness tier. A signed jug does not represent the whole invention of glassblowing. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: by c. 50 CE
date.basis: The museum attributes the jug to the first half of the first century CE; 50 is an approximate end to the context, not the first use of glassblowing.

events.statement: The Ennion workshop made a surviving multipart mold-blown glass jug.
events.caveats: The attribution and dating are museum judgments; the exact workshop location, purchaser and commissioning date remain uncertain.

evidence.supports: Identifies the signed jug, multipart mold method and first-half-first-century attribution.
